title: Research Methods in Computer Science
description: Research methodology for computer scientists: the meaning and types of research, the research problem, tools and methodology, data analysis, report and project writing, citation in APA and IEEE styles, journal writing, plagiarism and patents. Built from the CSC 476 course book and the 2022/23 examination (titled CSC 476: Research Methodology).

topics.title: The Meaning and Types of Research
topics.summary: Research is a systematic investigation to gain new knowledge, rising from data through information to knowledge, and its contribution must be original. Research is basic or applied, quantitative or qualitative, primary or secondary, and computer science research ranges from pure theory and descriptive studies to experiments, surveys and simulation.
subtopics: Meaning of research and the knowledge hierarchy
Knowledge, theories and areas of originality
Why do research; characteristics of good research
The dialectic: thesis, antithesis, synthesis
Basic and applied; quantitative and qualitative; primary and secondary
Classifications of computer science research

topics.title: Research Ideation and the Research Problem
topics.summary: Research ideas come from previous research, reading, observation, experience and discussion. The research problem is a clear statement of a concern to investigate; it should be specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time bound, and it is identified, formulated and stated in steps.
subtopics: Planning research and the research process
Sources of research ideas; phases of reading an article
Meaning and importance of a research problem
Characteristics and elements of a research problem
Identifying and formulating a research problem; common mistakes
Statement of the problem (Kerlinger's criteria)

topics.title: Research Tools and Methodology
topics.summary: Quantitative tools such as observation checklists, questionnaires and electronic data capture collect objective, standardized data; qualitative tools such as interviews and participant observation explore meanings and are triangulated. Methodology explains and justifies the methods chosen, using instruments such as programs, formal languages, systems and questionnaires.
subtopics: Quantitative data collection tools
Qualitative techniques and triangulation
Questionnaire design and types of question; sampling
Research method versus research methodology
Research instruments in computer science
Framework versus model

topics.title: Data Analysis
topics.summary: Analysis follows a plan written at the start of the project. Measurement scales (nominal, ordinal, continuous, ratio) decide the statistics: descriptive measures of central tendency and dispersion, and tests for association and causality such as chi-square, Pearson correlation and regression; qualitative analysis relies on coding, rigour, validity and reliability.
subtopics: The data analysis plan
Measurement scales: nominal, ordinal, continuous, ratio
Descriptive statistics and frequency distributions
Mean, median and measures of dispersion
Correlation, group comparison and regression
Qualitative analysis: rigour, validity and reliability

topics.title: Research Reports and Computer Science Project Writing
topics.summary: A research report has preliminary pages, an introduction, a literature review, methods, results and discussion. A computer science project is chosen with care, planned, proposed and written up in a standard format, with Chapter Two reviewing theory and related works and ending with the gap that justifies the study.
subtopics: Features of and reasons for research reports
Research report format
Choosing a computer science project
Planning, supervision and project proposals
Project format: preliminary pages and Chapter One
Chapter Two: the literature review

topics.title: Citation, Referencing and Journal Writing
topics.summary: Citation gives credit to the authors whose work is used. APA style uses author-date in-text citations and an alphabetical reference list, while IEEE uses numbered citations in square brackets. Journal articles should be prepared carefully for a suitable, indexed journal, and citations are measured by the h-index and i10-index.
subtopics: Citation and citation styles (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE)
APA reference list rules
APA in-text citation for one, two and more authors
Citing books, chapters, e-books, journal and newspaper articles
IEEE in-text citation and reference list
Writing for and choosing a journal; h-index and i10-index

topics.title: Plagiarism and Patents
topics.summary: Plagiarism is using another's words or ideas, or one's own earlier work, without due credit; it may be intentional, unintentional, of ideas, word-for-word, mosaic or self-plagiarism, and is avoided by good notes, paraphrasing, quoting, citation and checking tools. A patent grants exclusive rights to an innovation, usually for 20 years, after provisional and complete filing.
subtopics: Meaning of plagiarism
Types of plagiarism
Steps and tips to avoid plagiarism
Paraphrasing and quoting
Meaning of a patent
Filing a patent: provisional and complete specification
